analysis.title: Rates Vol Monitor: Shifting Tails Around a Benign Baseline
key_insights: USD and EUR implied rates vol hit cycle lows at the start of 2026, below GS fair value. AI disruption worries in February and then the US-Iran war pushed vol sharply higher, and it overshot fair value. GS sees a meaningful risk premium across both surfaces.
Short-vol strategies have had above-average returns this year despite the duration selloff. GS says the summer's high-yield, low-vol stretch is a useful playbook for the next year.
GS baseline is falling inflation, stable growth and a Fed that delivers fewer hikes than priced. That points to lower implied vol over the next year and supports vol-selling in 2027.

Energy risk has kept the inflation tail alive and produced the longest stretch of positive rates/vol correlation since 2021. AI-driven growth worries have recently replaced energy as the main yield driver, which has reduced sensitivity to oil.

GS sees limited upside to vol from yields or a supply shock. With 1y1y pricing up about 100 bps from summer lows, the push to implied vol from rising yields is largely exhausted. Even under extreme macro and yield stress, model fair value stays 0.5 to 1.0 bp/day below the prior cycle's peak.

Downside is the larger vol risk. AI slowdown fears have turned the rates/vol correlation sharply negative, so rate rallies rather than selloffs are likely to drive higher near-term vol. GS favors owning 6m to 1y expiries on 2y to 5y tails, with lower strikes giving the best balance of premium and return.

Payer/receiver skew was tilted to higher yields most of the year but has started to shift back. GS argues the market still overweights upside yield risk, because the Fed is less likely to fall behind the curve, the market prices more hikes than surveys imply, and tighter financial conditions are emerging. The tilt is less clearly toward lower yields than when yield levels were lower.
Although the baseline and elevated vol premium favor vol-selling, GS says broader risks favor overlaying short gamma with long vega strategies.

Midterm elections: vol usually carries a premium above fundamentals into midterms that fades after the result, whatever the outcome. GS economists see limited fiscal implications, so the current premium likely reflects post-election geopolitical escalation risk and concern about regulatory pressure on the AI buildout.

Other risks look contained. The debt ceiling is expected to bind in 1Q27 with historically limited impact, and vol markets are likely to look through tariff headlines such as the recent Canada tensions absent full re-escalation.

EUR vol also carries clear premium versus fundamentals. This year's rise in implied vol is about 70% of the 2022 spike, while yields and gas have covered about 30% and 10% of their 2022 rises. Tail risks are higher winter gas prices and French sovereign stress, and clarity on gas is needed to compress the premium fully.

Sovereign spread widening has introduced a speed limit to ECB tightening and brought back safe-haven flows. GS says core yield selloffs and spread widening are unlikely to be simultaneous sources of vol, and favors selling payers to fade 2027 ECB hike pricing.

Vol curve: as hike premium fades without cuts being priced, the tail curve typically steepens modestly. Only bull steepeners tend to invert the tail curve, parallel rallies add vol premium across the surface, and recession-type rallies build premium further out the curve. Deeper tail risks threaten relative-value curve trades.

Convexity hedging is a contained risk. About 95% of mortgages are locked in below current rates, so refinancing reopens only after a 75 to 150 bp yield drop. UST futures option gamma is centered near current yields with lower open interest, and callable issuance is near a standstill, so GS does not expect structural dealer vega supply to suppress long-dated vol.

macro_indicators.reading: Falling inflation, stable growth, Fed delivers fewer hikes than priced
macro_indicators.interpretation: Points to lower implied rates vol over the next year and supports vol-selling.

macro_indicators.reading: Yields must fall at least 75 to 150 bps
macro_indicators.interpretation: About 95% of mortgages are locked in below prevailing rates, so convexity hedging flows stay small in a selloff and refinancing flows stay muted.
History suggests limited vol impact from the negotiations.

macro_indicators.reading: Tightening concludes, then gradual non-recessionary cuts
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports a return at least part of the way toward late-2025 vol lows and vol-selling from attractive valuations.

trade_ideas.description: Own 6m to 1y expiry low-strike receivers on 2y to 5y rates as a hedge against an AI/growth scare
trade_ideas.rationale: Growth scares, especially if confirmed by weaker data, are the clearest route to higher vol, and lower strikes balance premium outlay and average return.

trade_ideas.description: Overlay short gamma (vol-selling) positions with long vega strategies
trade_ideas.rationale: The baseline and vol premium favor vol-selling, but broader risks favor adding long vega.

trade_ideas.description: Sell EUR payers to fade 2027 ECB hike pricing
trade_ideas.rationale: Sovereign stress introduces a speed limit to ECB hiking, and vol premium versus fundamentals is elevated.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher winter gas prices and renewed French sovereign stress could lift vol and hike pricing.

risk_factors: Acute AI/growth worries and weaker data, the clearest route to a further pickup in vol
Renewed geopolitical escalation and an energy price spike
Higher winter gas prices skewing European inflation risk to the upside
Renewed sovereign stress in France and tighter financing conditions
Post-midterm geopolitical escalation or regulatory pressure on the AI buildout
Deeper tail risks could hurt relative-value tail curve trades
charts_described: Exhibit 7 compares current moves in implied vol, 1y1y nominal yields and TTF gas as a share of their 2022 shock moves, with vol the furthest along
Exhibit 6 plots the average implied USD vol model residual into and out of US midterm elections, showing premium building before and fading after
Exhibit 4 shows the 1m correlation of 10y USD yields with oil, implied vol and an AI basket from Nov-25 to Nov-26
vol_and_positioning: USD and EUR implied vol both embed meaningful premium versus GS fair value across the surface, with EUR clearly overshooting fundamentals.
Payer/receiver skew was tilted to higher yields most of the year and has started to rebalance. GS thinks it still overweights upside yield risk.
Rates/vol correlation turned sharply negative on AI slowdown fears after the longest positive stretch since 2021.
Modest front-end rallies tend to flatten the tail curve most, while recession-type rallies steepen it by building premium further out.
Index-level convexity is close to zero, UST futures option gamma peaks around current yields and total open interest has been reduced.
The vol-selling richness signal (return-to-vol ratio from 1m5y, 1m10y and 1m30y gamma selling) is described as typically bullish for vol-selling at the current EUR model-implied richness.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict and energy supply risk kept the inflation tail alive and pushed rates vol higher
Post-midterm election geopolitical escalation risk is cited as a component of the current vol premium
Recent US-Canada trade tensions, with vol markets expected to look through headlines absent full tariff re-escalation
Renewed French sovereign stress could tighten financing conditions and lift EUR vol
Higher winter gas prices in Europe skew inflation risk up and could prompt more ECB tightening pricing

tension_points.bull_case: The baseline of falling inflation, stable growth and fewer Fed hikes than priced points to lower implied vol and supports vol-selling, with elevated premium and above-average vol-selling returns this year.
tension_points.bear_case: An AI/growth scare, especially if borne out by weaker data, would turn rate rallies into the main vol driver, and an energy spike remains a tail risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Emergence of acute AI/growth worries confirmed by weaker data, which GS calls the larger vol event than energy upside.

tension_points.bull_case: Normalizing inflation and ECB hike expectations are consistent with lower vol, and vol has risen more than gas prices or yields relative to 2022, leaving room for vol-selling and selling payers.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher winter gas prices would skew inflation up and bring more ECB tightening pricing, and renewed French sovereign stress could tighten financing conditions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A gas price spike into winter or renewed sovereign stress in France, since clarity on the gas outlook is needed to compress vol premium.
